verses.1: Early in the morning, the chief priests held a council with the elders and scribes and the whole Sanhedrin. They bound Jesus, led him away, and handed him over to Pilate.
verses.2: Pilate asked him, "Are you the King of the Jews?" Jesus answered him, "You say so."
verses.3: The chief priests brought many accusations against him.
verses.4: Pilate asked him again, "Do you give no answer? See how many charges they bring against you."
verses.5: But Jesus gave no further answer, so that Pilate was amazed.
verses.6: Now at the festival, Pilate used to release a prisoner for them, the one they requested.
verses.7: A man named Barabbas was in prison with the rebels, who had committed murder in the uprising.
verses.8: The crowd began to demand what they usually did.
verses.9: Pilate answered them, "Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?"
verses.10: For he knew that the chief priests had handed him over out of envy.
verses.11: But the chief priests incited the crowd to ask for Barabbas to be released to them instead.
verses.12: Pilate asked them again, "Then what would you like me to do with the one you call the King of the Jews?"
verses.14: Pilate said to them, "What evil has he done?" But they shouted all the more, "Crucify him!"
verses.15: Wanting to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them, and after flogging Jesus, he handed him over to be crucified.
verses.16: The soldiers led him into the courtyard of the palace, which was called the Praetorium, and they called the whole cohort together.
verses.17: They clothed him in a purple robe, and after weaving a crown of thorns, they placed it on his head.
verses.18: They began to greet him, "Hail, King of the Jews!"
verses.19: And they struck his head with a reed, spat on him, and knelt in mock worship.
verses.20: When they had finished mocking him, they removed the purple robe and put his own clothes back on him. Then they led him out to crucify him.
verses.21: They forced a certain Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.
verses.22: They brought him to Golgotha, which is translated as the Place of the Skull.
verses.23: They offered him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not take it.
verses.24: Then they crucified him and divided his clothes by casting lots for them.
verses.25: It was the third hour when they crucified him.
verses.26: And there was a written sign above him, which read: "The King of the Jews."
verses.27: They crucified two rebels with him, one on his right and one on his left.
verses.28: Those who passed by insulted him, shaking their heads and saying, "So you are the one who destroys the temple and rebuilds it in three days?
verses.29: Save yourself now, come down from the cross!"
verses.30: Likewise, the chief priests mocked each other along with the scribes, saying, "He saved others, but he cannot save himself.
verses.31: Let this Messiah, the King of Israel, come down from the cross now, so that we may see and believe." And those crucified with him also insulted him.
verses.32: It was the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
verses.33: At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out with a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?" which means, "My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?"
verses.34: Some of the bystanders who heard this said, "Look, he is calling for Elijah!"
verses.35: Someone ran, soaked a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink, saying, "Let's see if Elijah comes to take him down."
verses.36: Jesus uttered a loud cry and breathed his last.
verses.37: And the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
verses.38: The centurion who stood facing Jesus saw how he died and said, "Truly, this man was the Son of God."
verses.39: There were also women watching from a distance, among them Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
verses.40: These women had followed him when he was in Galilee and had cared for him, and there were many other women who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
verses.41: When evening had come, and it was the day of Preparation, which is the day before the Sabbath,
verses.42: Joseph of Arimathea, a respected member of the council and himself a man who was expecting the kingdom of God, came forward. He boldly went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
verses.43: Pilate was surprised that Jesus was already dead. He called the centurion and asked him if Jesus had already died.
verses.44: And having learned from the centurion, Pilate gave the body to Joseph.
verses.45: Joseph bought a linen shroud, took Jesus down, wrapped him in the shroud, and placed him in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock. He rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
verses.46: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where he was laid.

notes:
Notes
- v. 28: "Those who passed by insulted him..." — the original reads "καὶ οἱ παραπορευόμενοι ἐβλασφήμουν αὐτόν..." which is an accusative clause, here rendered as a narrative continuation for clarity.
raw:
[1] Early in the morning, the chief priests held a council with the elders and scribes and the whole Sanhedrin. They bound Jesus, led him away, and handed him over to Pilate.
[2] Pilate asked him, "Are you the King of the Jews?" Jesus answered him, "You say so."
[3] The chief priests brought many accusations against him.
[4] Pilate asked him again, "Do you give no answer? See how many charges they bring against you."
[5] But Jesus gave no further answer, so that Pilate was amazed.
[6] Now at the festival, Pilate used to release a prisoner for them, the one they requested.
[7] A man named Barabbas was in prison with the rebels, who had committed murder in the uprising.
[8] The crowd began to demand what they usually did.
[9] Pilate answered them, "Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?"
[10] For he knew that the chief priests had handed him over out of envy.
[11] But the chief priests incited the crowd to ask for Barabbas to be released to them instead.
[12] Pilate asked them again, "Then what would you like me to do with the one you call the King of the Jews?"
[13] They cried out again, "Crucify him!"
[14] Pilate said to them, "What evil has he done?" But they shouted all the more, "Crucify him!"
[15] Wanting to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them, and after flogging Jesus, he handed him over to be crucified.
[16] The soldiers led him into the courtyard of the palace, which was called the Praetorium, and they called the whole cohort together.
[17] They clothed him in a purple robe, and after weaving a crown of thorns, they placed it on his head.
[18] They began to greet him, "Hail, King of the Jews!"
[19] And they struck his head with a reed, spat on him, and knelt in mock worship.
[20] When they had finished mocking him, they removed the purple robe and put his own clothes back on him. Then they led him out to crucify him.
[21] They forced a certain Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.
[22] They brought him to Golgotha, which is translated as the Place of the Skull.
[23] They offered him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not take it.
[24] Then they crucified him and divided his clothes by casting lots for them.
[25] It was the third hour when they crucified him.
[26] And there was a written sign above him, which read: "The King of the Jews."
[27] They crucified two rebels with him, one on his right and one on his left.
[28] Those who passed by insulted him, shaking their heads and saying, "So you are the one who destroys the temple and rebuilds it in three days?
[29] Save yourself now, come down from the cross!"
[30] Likewise, the chief priests mocked each other along with the scribes, saying, "He saved others, but he cannot save himself.
[31] Let this Messiah, the King of Israel, come down from the cross now, so that we may see and believe." And those crucified with him also insulted him.
[32] It was the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
[33] At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out with a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?" which means, "My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?"
[34] Some of the bystanders who heard this said, "Look, he is calling for Elijah!"
[35] Someone ran, soaked a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink, saying, "Let's see if Elijah comes to take him down."
[36] Jesus uttered a loud cry and breathed his last.
[37] And the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
[38] The centurion who stood facing Jesus saw how he died and said, "Truly, this man was the Son of God."
[39] There were also women watching from a distance, among them Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
[40] These women had followed him when he was in Galilee and had cared for him, and there were many other women who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
[41] When evening had come, and it was the day of Preparation, which is the day before the Sabbath,
[42] Joseph of Arimathea, a respected member of the council and himself a man who was expecting the kingdom of God, came forward. He boldly went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
[43] Pilate was surprised that Jesus was already dead. He called the centurion and asked him if Jesus had already died.
[44] And having learned from the centurion, Pilate gave the body to Joseph.
[45] Joseph bought a linen shroud, took Jesus down, wrapped him in the shroud, and placed him in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock. He rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
[46] Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where he was laid.
